newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty drifts down, one-day depos rise.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty drifts down, one-day depos rise.

text.p: The Polish zloty drifted downward against the basket of currencies in thin early trade and was seen tracking dollar/mark movements thoughout the day.

Dealers said no large client orders were likely to appear today and the zloty eased from Wednesday's highs at around 1.93 percent from the parity rate on position shortening in order to benefit from holding zloty deposits over the weekend, during which the local currency is not devalued.
"The zloty slowly drifted down against the basket to 1.85 percent from parity but no strong selling or buying presuere was present," said Bogdan Stepkowski of ING Bank in Warsaw.
At 0815 GMT the zloty was at 1.87/1.84 percent from the parity rate, softer than 1.92/1.83 percent at 0700 GMT and Wednesday's close at 1.91/1.87 percent.

The zloty was at 2.7928/35 to the dollar, flat from 2.7920/50 at opening and down from 2.7825/40 on Thursday. It was at 1.8425/34 to the mark, down from opening's 1.8410/25 but up from yesterday's 1.8450/60.
On the money market one-day deposits rose as banks were reluctant to let out cash with only two trading days left on September's requried reserve period, which ends on Sunday.
At 0830 GMT overnight rates were at 19.50/20.50 percent up from 19.40/19.70 percent at 0635 GMT and 19.50/19.55 percent.
Tomorrow/next rates were at 20.20/21.10 percent, higher than 19.50/19.90 at opening and yesterday's 19.30/19.80.
Dealers said the high T/N rates could indicate that rates would rise on Friday as banks made final adjustments to reserve levels which they take into the month's last weekend.
They said the central bank's decision to refrain from staging a drainage operation today was another indication that the market may be tight tomorrow.
